measurement: In-process ASGI request elapsed time; includes real providers and DB, excludes local TCP and browser paint

habit_check.message: These habits passed local checks. Review them before adding.

drafts.cue: When you meet a tricky part of a familiar activity.
drafts.why: A clear signal can help you communicate that you need support without explaining first. This is a practical, adult-scaffolded support; its effectiveness has not been established.
steps: Choose a help signal, such as a gesture or picture.
Show your signal when you get stuck.
drafts.title: Signal when a task gets stuck
drafts.kid_hint: You can ask before a task feels too big.
drafts.strategy: Rehearse the signal during an easy activity, then respond first with help or a break. Do not require repeated tries or an explanation before helping. If the response is not useful, adapt your support or the task.
drafts.help_text: You can get help or take a break at any time. You can watch, try a smaller practice, or stop; you do not have to explain first.
drafts.description: Practice using a help or pause signal at a concrete obstacle in a familiar activity. Check first that the task and materials are accessible, and make sure help is available.
drafts.instruction: Show your help signal when you get stuck.
drafts.parent_setup: Choose a familiar, easy activity and check that the instructions and materials are accessible. Put a help or pause picture within reach, or agree on a gesture or AAC button. Be ready to respond right away.

parent_guidance.coach: Rehearse the signal during an easy activity. When you see it, offer help or a break first; investigate the obstacle together only if the child wants.
parent_guidance.if_hard: Offer help, a smaller practice, watching, declining, or a break without penalty. Help and breaks are never conditional on signaling or explaining.
parent_guidance.observe: Notice whether the signal brings useful assistance. Adapt your response or the task if needed; do not score feelings, compliance, or independence.
parent_guidance.prepare: Make sure the task and materials are accessible, place the help signal within reach, and be available to respond promptly.
